issues.legal_issue: The State Government may entertain a further revenue revision to examine the legality and propriety of an order made by a subordinate revenue authority in an earlier revision.
material_facts: A Sub-Divisional Officer exercised revisional powers over mutation entries, and the resulting orders were considered through further revenue proceedings, including a revision before the Commissioner.
A respondent then sought a further revision before the State Government, and the State Minister set aside the earlier orders and restored the mutation entries.
The appellant challenged the State Minister’s jurisdiction; the Supreme Court considered the maintainability of the further revision and did not decide the underlying land or mutation dispute.
issues.conclusion: The State Government had jurisdiction to entertain the further revision and examine the legality and propriety of the subordinate revenue authorities’ orders. The appeal was dismissed, without any opinion on the merits of the parties’ claims to the property.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5 and 11 of the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 place revenue officers under the State Government’s superintendence and make them subordinate to it. Section 257 empowers the State Government and specified revenue officers to call for and examine subordinate officers’ records and proceedings; the State Government’s revisional jurisdiction is concurrent with that of those officers and extends to orders made by them in revision. Section 259 preserves the State Government’s power under Section 257 even where an order is stated to be final or conclusive. The Court relied on Ishwar Singh v. State of Rajasthan, (2005) 2 SCC 334, in support of the conclusion that an earlier exercise of concurrent revisional power does not, in these circumstances, prevent the State Government from exercising its own power.

predicates.revenue_revision_proceeding: The matter arose in a proceeding to revise an order in revenue administration.
predicates.earlier_revision_by_subordinate_revenue_: A revenue authority subordinate to the State Government had made an order while exercising revisional powers.
predicates.state_government_controls_revenue_office: The State Government had superintendence and control over the revenue officers involved.
predicates.state_review_power_covers_subordinate_or: The governing scheme authorized the State Government to examine the legality and propriety of subordinate revenue officers’ orders and proceedings.

issues.definition: When a revenue revision follows an order made in revision by a subordinate revenue authority, and the State Government controls that authority and may review its orders, the State Government may entertain a further revision.
